Compare latent classes on an outcome not used to define them, correcting for classification error

Source: R/three-step.R
three_step.Rd

three_step() estimates how an outcome that was not used to define the classes differs between them: the mean of a numeric outcome in each class, or the probability of each category of a categorical one. The measurement model is held fixed, so the classes keep their meaning.

Comparing classes by modal assignment treats uncertain assignments as certain and biases the differences. The three-step methods correct for the classification error of the fitted model: step one is the fitted model, step two assigns each unit to its most probable class and measures how often each true class is assigned to another, and step three relates the outcome to the classes with those error rates built in. The default is the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars ("bch") weighting; the maximum-likelihood ("ml") method models the outcome given the true class instead. Both assume that the outcome and the assigned class are independent given the true class; the differences are associations, not effects of class membership.

Usage

three_step(
  x,
  data,
  outcome,
  level = c("individuals", "groups"),
  method = c("bch", "proportional", "modal", "ml"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  contrast = c("none", "pairs", "overall"),
  adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
  vcov_type = c("cluster", "independent"),
  variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  step_one = c("fixed", "estimated"),
  missing = c("error", "exclude")
)

Arguments

x

The fitted model whose classes are compared. It must have no membership covariates. Accepted:

  • a profile or class fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() (the default family = "profiles");

  • an lta() fit with its default homogeneous first-order transitions, invariant measurement and continuous or categorical indicators;

  • a trajectory model that classifies persons: mixture_regression() with class_level = "group", with or without random, fitted without membership covariates and without cluster.

Refused with latents_unsupported_three_step: a fit with membership covariates; the other multilpa() families (additive, dispersion and cross-level); an lta() fit with occasion-specific, second-order or covariate transitions, initial covariates, occasion-specific measurement, a stayer class, or ordinal or count indicators; a mixture regression that classifies observations; and a multilevel growth mixture (cluster). A fit with sampling weights raises latents_unsupported_weights, and one with a noise component latents_unsupported_noise.

data

The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order; columns shared with the fit are checked row by row, and a frame that does not match raises latents_bad_inference_data. For a trajectory model, the data the model was fitted to.

outcome

Name of the outcome column. It must not be an indicator of x, must have no infinite values, and must have no missing values unless missing = "exclude". A numeric column gives a mean in each class; a factor, character or logical column gives the probability of each category in each class. For level = "groups" the outcome must be constant within each group; for a trajectory model, within each person.

level

Which classes the outcome is related to:

  • "individuals" (default): the profiles (classes) of the observations;

  • "groups": the group classes of a two-level fit.

A trajectory model has person classes only: leave level at its default (the result reports level = "persons"); "groups" raises latents_bad_argument.

method

How step three relates the outcome to the classes:

  • "bch" (default): Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights. Each unit gets one weight per class, taken from the inverse of the classification-error matrix, and the class means are weighted means;

  • "ml": the maximum-likelihood step-three model. The assigned class is an indicator of the true class with the step-one error probabilities, and the outcome has a normal (numeric) or multinomial (categorical) distribution within each true class;

  • "proportional": each unit is weighted by its posterior class probabilities, without correction for classification error;

  • "modal": each unit counts fully in its most probable class, without correction.

The last two are the uncorrected comparisons the correction is judged against. See Methods.

ci_level

Confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

contrast

What is reported:

  • "none" (default): the outcome mean of each class (for a categorical outcome, the probability of each category in each class), with a confidence interval and no test;

  • "pairs": the difference between every pair of classes, each tested against zero;

  • "overall": one Wald test that every class has the same mean (the same category distribution).

adjust

Multiplicity correction of the p-values across the pairwise differences, giving p_adjusted. One of the stats::p.adjust() methods:

  • "BH" (default): Benjamini-Hochberg, controls the false discovery rate;

  • "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni": control the family-wise error rate;

  • "BY": Benjamini-Yekutieli, controls the false discovery rate under any dependence;

  • "none": no correction (p_adjusted equals p_value).

Used only with contrast = "pairs". With a binary outcome, its two complementary category rows count as one test per class pair; with more categories, every reported category difference enters the family.

vcov_type

Which units the sandwich variance treats as independent:

  • "cluster" (default): the fit's groups (the persons of a transition fit or a trajectory model), as the nesting requires. For a single-level fit every observation is its own group;

  • "independent": every observation, ignoring the nesting.

variance

The outcome variances of the "ml" model for a numeric outcome:

  • "varying" (default): one variance in each class;

  • "equal": one variance shared by the classes.

Supplying it with another method or with a categorical outcome raises latents_bad_argument.

step_one

Whether the standard errors include the uncertainty of the step-one estimates:

  • "fixed" (default): they condition on the step-one estimates;

  • "estimated": the uncertainty of the classification-error probabilities (and, under "ml", of the class sizes) is added to the step-three covariance. Available for lpa(), lca(), multilpa() and multilca() fits at either level, when their Wald inference is available and their measurement was estimated jointly. A transition fit, a trajectory model, a staged fit and a fit holding a measurement block fixed are refused.

See Step-one uncertainty.

missing

What to do with units whose outcome is missing:

  • "error" (default): a missing outcome value raises latents_bad_argument;

  • "exclude": the units without the outcome are left out of step three, as Latent GOLD's missing excludeall does. The step-one fit and its posteriors are unchanged, and the classification errors, weights and standard errors are those of the units analysed. This assumes the outcome is missing at random given the classes. At level = "groups" a group's outcome must be missing on all its rows or on none.

An outcome missing for every unit is refused under either value.

Value

A data frame of class latents_table (a data.frame that prints as a formatted table). Its rows depend on contrast:

  • contrast = "none": one row per class, or per class and category for a categorical outcome. Columns: level, method, class, category (categorical outcomes only), estimate (the class mean, or the probability of the category in the class), standard_error, conf_low, conf_high, variance (the outcome variance in the class; method = "ml" with a numeric outcome only) and effective_n (Kish's effective number of units behind the class's weights; under "ml" the expected number of units in the class). Means are not tested, and a probability's interval is formed on the logit scale;

  • contrast = "pairs": one row per pair of classes, or per pair and category. Columns: level, method, class, reference_class, category (categorical outcomes only), estimate (class minus reference), standard_error, statistic (the estimate over its standard error), p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low and conf_high;

  • contrast = "overall": one row. Columns: level, method, statistic (the Wald chi-square), df (K - 1 for a mean with K classes, (K - 1)(C - 1) for C categories) and p_value.

The attributes vcov_type and step_one record those choices; adjust is recorded on a pairs result and variance on a numeric ML result with contrast = "none".

Errors: latents_unsupported_three_step, latents_unsupported_weights and latents_unsupported_noise for a fit the correction does not cover (see x); latents_bad_outcome for an outcome that is an indicator of x (also of class multilpa_indicator_reused), that varies within a group or person where one value is needed, or that takes a single category (under "ml", a single value); latents_bad_data when data has no column named by outcome; latents_bad_inference_data when data is not the fit's data; latents_bad_argument for any other invalid argument; latents_inseparable_classes when the classification-error matrix cannot be inverted or a single class is asked for a contrast; and latents_too_few_groups when there are no more independent units than classes. Warnings: latents_bch_out_of_range, latents_boundary and latents_small_classes, described under Methods and Standard errors, and latents_unconverged when the "ml" model did not converge. latents-conditions describes each class.

Methods

BCH gives each observation one weight per class, the row of the inverse classification-error matrix for its assigned class, and takes weighted means. With method = "ml" the assigned class is an indicator of the true class with the step-one error probabilities, and the outcome is normal within each true class (a multinomial distribution for a categorical outcome), with the class sizes fixed at the average posteriors, as in Latent GOLD's step-three model. The likelihood is maximised from a fixed set of starts plus twenty seeded random ones, so the result does not depend on the caller's seed; the global maximum is not guaranteed. ML depends on the within-class outcome distribution: skewness or a wrong equal-variance constraint can bias the means, and BCH is less sensitive to that.

A categorical outcome is described by its probability in each class. BCH weights can be negative, so with poorly separated classes a share can fall outside 0 to 1; it is then reported without an interval or test, with a latents_bch_out_of_range warning. The ML probabilities stay in range; where the BCH shares do not, the ML maximum usually sits on the bound and is reported without standard errors, with a latents_boundary warning.

On an lta() fit, level = "individuals" uses one row per occasion and relates the outcome to the profile at that occasion, with the group-clustered variance accounting for the repeated occasions. It is a marginal profile-outcome analysis, not a model of outcome effects on transitions.

Standard errors

The variance is a sandwich over the G independent units (the groups, or the observations under vcov_type = "independent") with the G / (G - 1) small-sample factor. It needs more units than classes; with as many or fewer, the analysis is refused (latents_too_few_groups). A class carried by one unit (Kish's effective number of units carrying it below 1.5) has no standard error: its interval and the contrasts involving it are NA, with a latents_small_classes warning.

Step-one uncertainty

With step_one = "fixed" the intervals ignore the uncertainty of the classification-error probabilities, which lowers their coverage when classification is uncertain. "estimated" adds the first-order contribution of the step-one covariance, with the data and modal assignments held fixed; the estimates are unchanged, the standard errors and intervals grow, and the tests use the corrected covariance. The first-stage contribution uses its model-based observed information, even when the step-three sandwich is clustered; it does not add a robust first-stage covariance for residual dependence outside the fitted model. The correction is a large-sample one: in a small, poorly separated sample the intervals still cover less than the nominal level. The modal method is unaffected, as it uses no posteriors. A staged fit or a fit with a held measurement block does not carry the measurement covariance needed by this correction; use step_one = "fixed" to report inference conditional on that measurement. Neither option includes the uncertainty of having selected the class solution.

See also

r3step() for covariates of class membership; fit_staged(); get_results(x, "classification_errors") for the error matrix the correction uses.

Examples

set.seed(11)
group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10)
truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5)
example_data <- data.frame(
  g = group,
  a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,
                n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1)
# The mean of `y` in each class, then the difference between the classes.
three_step(fit, example_data, "y")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n
#> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  -----------
#>     1  -0.069  [-0.463,  0.325]  0.20       182.74
#>     2   9.972  [ 9.531, 10.412]  0.22       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs")
#> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH)
#> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------
#>     2   1       10.04  [9.37, 10.72]  <.001   <.001
# A categorical outcome: its probability in each class.
example_data <- transform(example_data, passed = y + rnorm(400, sd = 6) > 5)
three_step(fit, example_data, "passed")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  Category  Probability        95% CI     SE  Effective n
#> -----  --------  -----------  ------------  -----  -----------
#>     1  FALSE            0.80  [0.73, 0.85]  0.030       182.74
#>     1  TRUE             0.20  [0.15, 0.27]  0.030       182.74
#>     2  FALSE            0.17  [0.12, 0.23]  0.030       170.37
#>     2  TRUE             0.83  [0.77, 0.88]  0.030       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "passed", contrast = "overall")
#> Distal outcome: equal across classes (bch, Wald)
#> 
#>  Wald  df      p
#> -----  --  -----
#> 99.11   1  <.001
# An outcome missing for some units: they are left out of step three.
example_data <- transform(example_data, y_seen = replace(y, seq_len(25), NA))
three_step(fit, example_data, "y_seen", missing = "exclude")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n
#> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  -----------
#>     1  -0.012  [-0.435,  0.412]  0.22       167.09
#>     2   9.949  [ 9.496, 10.402]  0.23       162.74
